text:
maya: heads-up — we had 3 OOMs on prod-runtime-8 this morning. All tied to very long sessions (approx 100k-140k tokens).

maya: symptoms: KV cache kept growing and never reclaimed, fragmentation high, paging kicked in and then allocs failed. oom-bot alerted at 06:12.

sam: can you paste the runtime logs / perf snapshot? any kernel-selection jumps or big batching spikes?

maya: attaching snippets below (trimmed):
```
KVCache::alloc() requested=2.1GB free=1.8GB frag_ratio=0.78
kv_page_manager: paged_out=42MB paged_in=120MB io_wait_ms=320
kernel_switch: from=fp16-opt to=quant32 at step=4783
batcher: active_queue=64 avg_latency_ms=210
```

alex: looks like fragmentation ratio is brutal (0.78). That + ongoing longctx appends explains steady growth. Were there any recent changes to `kv_reuse_threshold` or slab coalescing?

li: I rolled the compaction heuristics two weeks ago but it shouldn't affect coalescing logic. We did change the kernel selection fallback window (smaller to prefer quant kernels) — maybe that changed allocation patterns.

ciara: added a new metric `kv_frag_ratio` last week to prod telemetry, here's the alert history: frag_ratio spiked over 0.6 two hours before the first OOM.

jen: oom-bot: Incident created — group=eng-runtime, sev=2, nodes=prod-runtime-8/9/11.

maya: immediate mitigations applied: reduced per-session max_kv_slots from 64k -> 32k (hotpatch), enabled `kv_autoshrink: true` with aggressive target reclaim 20s. Also routed sessions > 80k tokens to a smaller model variant as fallback.

alex: good. What's the plan for a durable fix?

sam: proposals: (1) smart eviction: prefer evicting fragmented slabs first; (2) background compaction that merges adjacent free slabs when CPU underutilized; (3) on-kernel-switch re-evaluate cache layout to avoid leaving many small free fragments; (4) early degrade for long contexts (stream-only mode / stateless generation) when frag_ratio > 0.5.

li: I can prototype background compaction that runs per-shard at low priority. But risk: compaction increases short-term CPU and can degrade p99 latency. We'll gate by `cpu_idle_ms` threshold.

ciara: add this to telemetry: emit `kv_compaction_runs`, `compaction_cpu_ms`, `evicted_slabs_count`. We need a signal to trigger rollback if tail latency goes up.

maya: also looking at batching heuristics — we saw a batch size spike to 64 with avg seq_len 40k once a long session was admitted. We should clamp batch size by token-based criteria, not just request count.

alex: agreed. Token-clamped batching: max_tokens_per_batch = 256k. If incoming queue would exceed that, flush early. That will keep memory headroom stable.

sam: quick hotfix we can ship today: (A) token-clamped batching default, (B) lower `max_kv_slots` for hosted tier aggressor flag, (C) KV autoshrink backoff tuning. I can prepare PR.

jen: deploy-bot: rolling hotfix to prod-runtime pool in 3m. Canarying on 2 nodes.

maya: post-deploy we should run a repro harness that simulates 120k token sessions and measure kv_frag_ratio, compaction effectiveness, and p99 latency. Sam please add the harness scenario to perf-tests.

sam: on it. I'll add a job that spins up 5 clients producing 100-130k token dialogues over 2 hours. Will capture: oom events, kv_alloc traces, kernel selection logs, and batch size history.

li: long term, we should adjust kernel-selection heuristics so quant kernels don't create many tiny allocations. Maybe prefer larger-slab allocators for quant fallback codepath.

ciara: also recommend implementing a soft-fallback policy: if kv_frag_ratio > 0.6 for > 5m, automatically route new long sessions to `redwood-small-llm` or enable `stateless_streaming=true` for those sessions. That prevents cluster OOM cascade.

maya: agreed. Also add a ticket to add an automatic circuit-breaker that prevents admission of sessions likely to exceed headroom — compute estimated kv_slots = sum(seq_len / kv_slot_per_token). If estimated + current_used > headroom * 0.85, reject or queue.

alex: one more thought: retries & graceful degrade. If a request fails with OOM during generation we should attempt 1 retry with: lower `max_new_tokens`, `use_kv_reuse=false` (force fresh context), and `fallback_model=redwood-small`. This can reduce customer-visible failures.

sam: agreed, will add that to runtime error handling. Also log retry_reason with a `oom_kv_frag` tag.

maya: timeline: ship hotfix (token-clamp + autoshrink tuning) now. Prototype compaction in two sprints. Circuit-breaker + soft-fallback in one sprint after compaction.

jen: deploy-bot: hotfix applied to canaries, monitoring for 15m.

ciara: initial canary metrics: kv_frag_ratio on canaries dropped from 0.72 -> 0.45 after autoshrink + clamp. batch token budget stabilized, p99 latency +10ms.

maya: that's promising. Keep monitoring. I'll open a postmortem draft once we confirm there are no remaining OOMs. Thanks everyone. :heart:

oom-bot: Alert cleared for prod-runtime-8 (condition: kv_frag_ratio < 0.5 for 20m).
